chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from al-Sayyari from Muhammad ibn Jumhur from whom he mentioned from Ibn Abi Ya'fur who said:

Testimony was required of him, so he gave it before Abu Yusuf the judge. Abu Yusuf said to him: 'What do I say about you, O Ibn Abi Ya'fur, while you have been going on as I knew you to be, except truthful, long-prayerer? But that specific trait.' He said: 'And what is it?' He said: 'Your leaning towards al-teraffudh.' So Ibn Abi Ya'fur wept until his tears flowed. Then he said: 'O Abu Yusuf, you have attributed me to a people of whom I fear I may not be.' He said: 'And he validated his testimony.'

key_terms.اَلتَّرَفُّضِ: Al-teraffudh (leaning towards luxury/worldliness or a specific sect/trait)
key_terms.طَوِيلَ اَللَّيْلِ: Long-prayerer (one who prays long in the night)

ai.seo_question: What was the reason for Ibn Abi Ya'fur's emotional reaction when Abu Yusuf questioned his testimony?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic principle that a single flaw (khalalah) does not necessarily invalidate a witness's testimony if their overall integrity (sadaqah) remains intact, as demonstrated by Abu Yusuf's acceptance of Ibn Abi Ya'fur. The narrative underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between minor defects and fundamental dishonesty, reflecting the nuanced approach to 'adalah' (justice/integrity) in legal testimony.
